pick.angle: Lead with Pydantic’s 812.6 million package downloads versus 28.9 thousand GitHub stars in the dated snapshot, then explain how dependencies and distribution channels create gaps—and why developers should check both signals alongside recent commits and issue response.
pick.why_share: Developers and maintainers can share a concrete, sourced explanation of why neither stars nor downloads alone establishes adoption or quality, with a practical checklist for evaluating tools without dismissing popular projects as hype.

outline:
- **Title: "Pydantic: 812.6 million downloads, 28.9 thousand GitHub stars"**
- **Opening answer block, within 50 words:** Lead with Pydantic's 812.6 million downloads versus 28.9 thousand stars. State that dependencies and distribution channels help explain the gap, and that neither measure alone tells developers which tool is better.
- **## What was counted:** Establish the October 3, 2026 snapshot: 230 directory tools with npm or PyPI packages whose registry pages link to their own GitHub repos. Name the npm downloads API and pypistats; specify the last-30-days window. Downloads include CI and mirrors, so they are not user counts.
- **## Dependencies collect downloads without stars:** Explain repeated installs in builds. Use one small table with Pydantic, OpenAI Python (284.2 million downloads, 31.7 thousand stars), and MCP Python SDK (219.0 million, 24.5 thousand). Note Pydantic's approximately 28,000 downloads per star without treating the ratio as a quality score.
- **## Package downloads miss other distribution channels:** Contrast n8n's 206.5 thousand stars and 384.9 thousand downloads with Langflow's 155.5 thousand stars and 40.1 thousand downloads. Explain that these self-hosted platforms are mostly installed through Docker or their own installers; low package counts do not establish low use or hype.
- **## How to use both signals when choosing a tool:** Recommend checking stars and downloads alongside recent commits and issue response. Check distribution before interpreting a gap. Introduce [our downloads page](https://agentoolrank.com/downloads), explicitly identifying AgentoolRank as Jason T.'s directory of open-source AI agent tools ranked by live GitHub activity.
- **Closing lines:** Note that the same data is queryable over MCP/API with a [free key](https://agentoolrank.com/api-key). Invite corrections: "If a package mapping is wrong, tell us." Sign "Jason T." End with the short disclosure: "I make AgentoolRank; the downloads page is ours."
